title: Checks for missing blank lines between methods of a class.
summary: PEP 8 recommends exactly one blank line between methods of a class. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for missing blank lines between top level functions and classes.
summary: PEP 8 recommends exactly two blank lines between top level functions and classes. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous blank lines.
summary: PEP 8 recommends using blank lines as follows: - No more than two blank lines between top-level statements. - No more than one blank line between non-top-level statements. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.

title: Checks for extraneous blank line(s) after function decorators.
summary: There should be no blank lines between a decorator and the object it is decorating. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.
message_templates: Blank lines found after function decorator ({})

title: Checks for missing blank lines after the end of function or class.
summary: PEP 8 recommends using blank lines as follows: - Two blank lines are expected between functions and classes - One blank line is expected between methods of a class. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.
message_templates: Expected 2 blank lines after class or function definition, found ({})

title: Checks for 1 blank line between nested function or class definitions.
summary: PEP 8 recommends using blank lines as follows: - Two blank lines are expected between functions and classes - One blank line is expected between methods of a class. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle. It is in preview.
message_templates: Expected 1 blank line before a nested definition, found 0

title: `…()` got some positional-only arguments passed as keyword arguments: ….
summary: Emitted when positional-only arguments have been passed as keyword arguments. Remove the keywords for the affected arguments in the function call. pylint calls it positional-only-arguments-expected.
message_templates: `{}()` got some positional-only arguments passed as keyword arguments: {}

title: Invalid usage of field(), ….
summary: The dataclasses.field() specifier should only be used as the value of an assignment within a dataclass, or within the make_dataclass() function. pylint calls it invalid-field-call.
